findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?', so the guard is never invoked by AMS
findings.body: The conditional-inclusion hook is defined as `def include_website_name` (line 153), but ActiveModel::Serializers dispatches guards by the exact name `include_#{attribute}?` — every other guard in this same file (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, include_card_image_badge?, and the ones generated by the untrusted_attributes macro at lines 26-32) ends with a question mark. Because the dispatcher looks up `include_website_name?` and does not find it, it falls back to "always include", so the intended `website.present?` check is dead code and `website_name` is serialized for every user — including a `website_name: null` entry for users with no website at all. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and add a test asserting `website_name` is absent from the JSON when the website is blank.

findings.title: website_name is not registered as an untrusted attribute, leaking hidden website data for TL0 profiles
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which suppresses it when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. a TL0 user's profile viewed by an anonymous visitor — an anti-scraping/privacy measure). The new `website_name` attribute is declared as a plain attribute and its include guard only checks `website.present?`, so for a restricted TL0 profile the serializer omits `website` but still emits `website_name`, which contains the very data that was supposed to be hidden — the website's host, and even the full path when the domain matches the instance. This partially defeats the untrusted-attributes protection. `website_name` should be added to the `untrusted_attributes` list (replacing the hand-written guard), and the spec's `untrusted_attributes` list at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 should include `:website_name` so the regression is caught — currently the TL0/anonymous test passes while the leak exists.

findings.title: Same-domain check is asymmetric: instance apex + website 'www.' subdomain does not show the path
findings.body: The final branch only tests `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, i.e. whether the WEBSITE host is a parent domain of the instance host. It never checks the reverse direction. Concretely: on an instance at `example.com`, a user whose website is `http://www.example.com/my-page` gets only `www.example.com` displayed (path hidden), while on an instance at `www.example.com` a website of `http://example.com/my-page` gets the full `example.com/my-page` displayed. Since the PR's intent is to show the full path when the website lives on the same domain as the forum, and the code explicitly treats sibling subdomains (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, line 144-146) as same-domain, the apex-instance case is an inconsistency that will produce confusingly different behavior for equivalent setups. The check should also cover `website_host.ends_with?("." << discourse_host)`.
